Verb tense tells you when something happened. Find the time clue in the sentence, then match the verb to it.
Think of it like a time stamp on a photo. Before you pick the verb, read the time stamp.
Here's the method. Circle the time clue. It could be a date, the word since, the phrase by the time, or the tense of the other verbs. Then pick the tense that matches.
A past date means past tense. In nineteen sixty nine, astronauts landed on the moon. Nineteen sixty nine is over, so landed, not land.
Since means has or have. Since twenty twenty, the museum has won three awards. Since reaches from then all the way up to now.
Trap alert. Since twenty twenty, the museum won three awards. Plain past doesn't reach up to now. Since needs has or have.
By the time, in the past, means had. By the time the rescue team arrived, the storm had ended. Had marks the earlier of two past events.
And a general fact stays in the present. This tool measures quality of life. It's true now, so use the present tense.
Let's try an SAT style question. The researcher blank Saturn's rings when she made a discovery. Studies, was studying, has studied, or will study?
Made is past, and she was in the middle of it when the discovery happened. So the answer is was studying.
Trap alert. Studies is in the present tense. It clashes with made, which is in the past tense. Match the other verbs in the sentence.
